newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes steady in late Asia, June Masila firm.
newsitem.headline: Crudes steady in late Asia, June Masila firm.

text.p: Crude oil prices stayed mostly steady in Asia on Thursday, with physical trading in Gulf crudes mostly dull apart from a June Masila which was believed sold to a European major at a firm premium, traders said.
The market was quiet in the absence of fresh news to provide the market with direction, they said.
At 0805 GMT June cash Brent was assessed at $17.95/18.00 per barrel, slightly firmer than late U.S. trading levels of $17.85/17.95.
In spreads, Brent/Dubai was assessed mostly unchanged from late U.S. trading levels.
June Brent/Dubai was assessed at $1.45/1.50 for June and $1.50/1.60 for July.
In the physical market, a 500,000-barrel June Masila was believed sold to a European major at a premium of 15 cents to the official selling price by a Western trader.
It is the first report of a deal for June-loading cargoes.
A May Oman was believed to have been sold by a European oil company at a sharp discount to the official selling price, leaving no more Oman cargoes available for the month.
In Asian crudes, May Tapis was offered at published quotes plus 75 cents.
The potential seller said firm bids had yet to emerge, but that the crude was attracting some buying interest.
Some other traders said bids were likely to emerge at premium levels of about 50 cents.
The seller said about two Tapis cargoes were still available for May.
